body:
**Note (correctness): Stale temp cleanup no longer matches new temp names**

`remove()` still deletes `<cursorTrack>.tmp`, but writes now use `<target>.<pid>.<uuid>.tmp`. A crash mid-write leaves a uniquely named temp file that nothing removes, so these accumulate in `.kaipu`. The `.tmp` rm is now dead code. Consider a startup sweep or removing the dead line.

**Note (other): chmod-based failure test fails when run as root**

`chmod(dir, 0o500)` doesn't block writes for root (e.g. some Docker CI). The test would then see the write succeed and fail. Also skip when `process.getuid?.() === 0`.
